title: The Horse and the Bird would Stand Outsmarted!
paragraphs: Vēḷaṉ was returning home on his fleeting horse Eager as he was to see his beloved wife.
The tears shed by the sky would bring happiness to the peasants, While Vēḷaṉ’s return alone could infuse life into his woman.

The flower doesn’t wither If the colourful beetle fails to visit to relish its honey, While the young woman’s heart might turn into a turbulent earthquake If the horse carrying Vēḷaṉ failed to be back home. She might breathe like a storm and writhe like a worm.

The horse should understand that and gallop towards its destination Without taking a break in between, Without any hindrances on the way home. Vēḷaṉ spurred the horse on; The horse sped like a bird’s flight; And it was the bird From which he took the cue for his flight home.
When Tolkāppiyar says The horse matched the speed of the bird, We cannot help entertaining a doubt.
The bird flying in the sky should rapidly flutter its wing to fly fast, And the horse has to gallop to reach home, Both of which might take quite some time.
But Vēḷaṉ’s heart Burning with passion intense for his lady Could be home to her The moment he thought he should be home.

> No sojourn does the hero’s journey across the parched tract mark > As he is homeward after his mission accomplished; > For he had at his possession > A sturdy horse swift as a bird > That abides at his service > As does his benignant heart.
